label: Ultrafiltered milk
note: Ultra-filtered milk is not milk with protein powder added: the proteins stay in the milk and part of the water, lactose and minerals goes out through the membrane. fairlife says it takes out about half the sugar and uses no added protein powder.

about.text: Milk pushed through a fine membrane that keeps the proteins and lets much of the water, lactose and minerals through, so it ends up with more protein and less sugar than ordinary milk. Sold in the US mostly as fairlife.

how.text: The milk is separated, the skim part is pushed through a membrane that holds back the proteins, and the cream and the minerals that went through are put back, so the milk keeps its fat and gets denser in protein.

steps.note: Cold, through a membrane that holds back the proteins (80 % casein, 20 % whey, as in milk) and fat and passes water, lactose and some minerals.

steps.name: return minerals
steps.note: The lactose-rich stream is split again by nanofiltration and reverse osmosis, and the minerals go back.
For the lactose left over; it is on the label.
